instructor_brief: Students review the seven-frame voting story as a story author, first-time reader, and critical editor. Each prepares an account, questions a peer in a roundtable, then revises their own explanation. Use 2 groups of 3 learners for 15 minutes.

material.title: Who gets a vote?
material.source_context: A seven-part story narrows the US population to voters in competitive Senate states. The voting data refer to 2010; the story concerns the 2014 election. Area represents population, not geographic area.
material.author: Keith Collins & Greg Giroux · Bloomberg

student_roles.preparation_question: What message does the seven-frame story communicate? Explain how changing area supports that message.
student_roles.exchange_action: Present the intended message. Ask {peer} which visual choice makes that message clear.

student_roles.preparation_question: Compare the first and final frames. What does area represent? Name one step that needs a clearer explanation.
student_roles.exchange_action: Explain one difficult reading. Ask {peer} to point to the label or visual choice that resolves it.

student_roles.preparation_question: Which step supports the claim about a small voting population? State one claim the story cannot establish.
student_roles.exchange_action: Test one claim against the source. Ask {peer} to narrow any claim the visual cannot support.

generation_mode: Codex authoring uses the supplied prompts and catalogue. The local webpage uses four method-specific blueprints; no model API is connected.
shared_scenario: An editorial meeting: the story author, first-time reader, and critical editor review the visual for publication.

instructor_responsibilities.prepare: Clarify the editorial scenario and each role’s responsibility.
instructor_responsibilities.roundtable: Listen to the exchange; probe a claim that needs support.
instructor_responsibilities.revise: Debrief the different positions before students revise.
